name: Pfarrkirche St. Jakob am Arlberg
kurzbeschreibung: The baroque Parish Church of St. James in St. Anton am Arlberg is the oldest sanctuary in the upper Stanzer Valley and a cherished station on the Way of St. James.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Parish Church of St. James (Pfarrkirche St. Jakob am Arlberg) is the oldest documented church in the upper Stanzer Valley, perched picturesquely on a sunny slope in the hamlet of St. Jakob near St. Anton am Arlberg. As early as the 13th century, a Romanesque chapel stood here, providing shelter and spiritual solace to pilgrims and travellers preparing to cross the treacherous Arlberg Pass. The current church was constructed between 1773 and 1778 in the late baroque style by master builder Franz Singer of Götzens. Featuring an elegant onion-domed steeple, classical facade proportions, and a bright, harmonious interior, it stands as an enduring cultural beacon in the Arlberg mountains.

Route & Requirements

Visiting the church is easily combined with an enjoyable valley walk or a leg along the Tyrolean Way of St. James (Jakobsweg), which passes right by the churchyard. From central St. Anton am Arlberg, a paved and largely traffic-free pedestrian path leads to St. Jakob in approximately twenty to thirty minutes of gentle walking. The trail has minimal elevation gain and is ideal for walkers of all ages, families with prams, and senior visitors. The church is open during daylight hours, offering pilgrims a peaceful sanctuary for contemplation.

Visiting & Getting There

St. Anton am Arlberg is a major rail hub served regularly by international Railjet and Eurocity trains. Local valley buses run frequently between St. Anton station and St. Jakob, stopping directly near the church. Drivers will find limited parking spaces near the village cemetery. The church is accessible year-round without admission fees. Traditional pilgrim stamps for the credential are available in the entrance narthex.

Tips

Take time to study the colourful ceiling frescoes by Tyrolean artist Johann Mittermayr, portraying the life and miracles of St. James the Greater. The high altar holds a fine late-Gothic wood-carved statue of St. James with his pilgrim staff and scallop shell, dating back to the early 16th century. After your visit, enjoy the peaceful alpine views from the churchyard across the Stanzer Valley towards the rugged Lechtal Alps.
